answer_text: The evidence indicates that retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) does not consistently improve the factual accuracy of LLM-generated answers; the impact varies significantly by domain and benchmark. In some cases, RAG yields substantial improvements in accuracy, while in others, it results in no measurable change or even a slight decrease. Specifically, RAG improved accuracy on LawFactQA [S033, 1492-2672], PopCultureQA [S027, 1614-2911; S066, 1708-3093], and NewsTruthQA [S100, 1848-3145]. However, RAG did not make answers measurably more accurate on SciFactBench [S015, 0-744] or GeoFacts [S098, 0-768], and it resulted in a slight decrease in accuracy on HistoryQuest [S040, 1627-2889].
